Squared Text Generator

Boxed capital letters that paste into any plain text field

Boxed capitals, with no lowercase anywhere

Each letter sits inside its own outlined box, which is why squared text reads like something stencilled onto a crate rather than written in a sentence. The characters come from the Enclosed Alphanumeric Supplement, a block Unicode added for exactly this kind of label. It is twenty-six uppercase tiles and nothing else, so whatever you type comes out capitalised, and any digit in your text stays an ordinary digit because squared numbers were never encoded.

Nothing here is a font. Your text stays text; each letter is swapped for a different codepoint that happens to be drawn with a border, which is how the look survives a copy into a field that offers no styling at all. Good for a status tag at the front of a forum title or a channel name meant to read as a placard. Older Android system fonts miss part of this block and draw an empty rectangle instead.

Also searched as: square text, boxed letters, square letter generator.

Where Squared text works, and where it does not

WorksVery widely supported — these are long-standing characters and most fonts on most devices have them. Watch outSome Android system fonts miss the lowercase enclosed letters and draw an empty box instead.

Squared questions

Why does my lowercase come out as capitals?

Because there is no lowercase set to map to. The Enclosed Alphanumeric Supplement gives Unicode one squared alphabet and it is the uppercase one, so lowercase input is pointed at the same twenty-six tiles. If mixed case has to survive, small caps or one of the maths alphabets will keep the distinction that this style cannot.

Can I square numbers as well as letters?

No. Unicode has circled digits and parenthesized digits, but it never encoded a squared nought through nine, so numbers pass straight through unchanged. A model number comes out half boxed and half plain. If the digits matter visually, the bubble style covers the full range and gets you closer to an even line.

What is the difference between this and the black squared style?

Weight. This one draws an outline around the letter and leaves the middle open, so it stays legible at small sizes. The negative squared set inverts that: a solid tile with the letter knocked out of it, much darker in a run of ordinary text. Both live in the same neighbourhood of Unicode and share the uppercase-only limit.
